utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Good afternoon to everybody in and around the courtroom. Mr. Registrar, will you please call the case.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Good afternoon, Your Honours. Good afternoon to everyone in and around the courtroom. This is case number IT-04-81-T, The Prosecutor versus Momcilo Perisic. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Thank you very much. Could we have the appearances for the day starting with the Prosecution.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: Good afternoon, Your Honours. Barney Thomas, Dan Saxon, and Carmela Javier for the Prosecution.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Thank you very much. And for the Defence.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Good afternoon, Your Honours. Good afternoon to everyone in and around the courtroom. Mr. Perisic is represented today by Novak Lukic, Gregor Guy-Smith, Tina Drolec, and Mr. Zorko.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Thank you so much. Good afternoon to you, Mr. Simic. Again, a warning that you already know, to tell the truth and whole truth and nothing else but the truth. Thank you so much. Mr. Saxon.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Good afternoon, Your Honours. Good afternoon to everyone in the courtroom.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: Our Honour, can we excuse the witness for a moment, please. I have a motion to make.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Mr. Simic, you are asked to please excuse us for a short while.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Saxon.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: Your Honour, this is an application to use a photograph that falls into the category of fresh evidence with General Simic. And we have some copies. We've already given a copy to Defence counsel and a copy for General Perisic, and I've got several more copies here which can I show to the Chamber, if the Chamber would like to see them. It is 65 ter 431002. It was on the Prosecution's 65 ter list. It was not tendered into evidence. We had an agreed fact related to this photograph. This photograph shows the area of the Kozluk massacre, part one of the events related to Srebrenica in July 1995. Shows the Drina river, and the execution site, and the burial site for approximately --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Just before you carry on. You've got s photograph, Mr. Lukic?

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, yes, Your Honour, I do.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Are we getting copies? Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: Your Honour, Your Honours were at this site during the site visit last year, and there --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Yeah. Carry on.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: And in the work book for the site visit, around page 94, there is some satellite imagery of this particular site. In his testimony, this witness referred to the heightened security of the VJ border patrols. This was at transcript page 10095 on last Thursday. The witness testified with regard to the Srebrenica events: "Therefore, it was important to take measures of heightened security along the state border, so that such armed persons would not cross the border or, rather, even if they were to cross the border, that we act in accordance with the border service rules."

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Okay. Can I just find out something from the Defence? What's the attitude of the Defence, Mr. Lukic?

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: Can we have a second? [Microphone not activated]

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: I believe -- I believe in response to your question, Your Honour, our position is -- is that based upon what we've heard thus far, unless it's going any further, that the purpose for which Mr. Saxon is suggesting that this photograph be shown to the witness does not fall into the area of impeachment. And I don't believe that -- that the justification he has given falls within the jurisprudence as to why it's being offered only after the conclusion of its case, especially in light of some of the other things he said with regard to us having been in the area and at a site visit.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Sorry, yeah. That is why I stopped him because I thought he was going outside the bounds of the jurisprudence. But I'm also not understanding you. Can you just say in one sentence, are you opposed to the application or not?

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: We are opposed to the application.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Thank you. Thank you. Mr. Saxon, if you can motivate your application now that it is being opposed within the jurisprudence of the Tribunal.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: Your Honour, the Prosecution wishes to use this photograph for the purposes of impeachment of the witness only, with respect to the witness's evidence given about the -- his -- what he described as the measures of heightened security along the state border.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Okay.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: In addition -- if I may carry on. In addition, with respect to a document that was tendered through the witness, which document is now Exhibit D227. It was discussed with the witness at pages 10101 to 10102 of the transcript on Thursday. And on the second page of this document, there is information provided by a VJ border unit regarding, inter alia, a group of Muslims who were, at that time, in Kozluk village. And so the Prosecution wishes to use this photograph to question the witness about what these so-called heightened measures really were.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: And do you say that this photograph was in the Prosecution's 65 ter list?

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: It was 65 ter 4310.02. And if you've like, I could provide the disclosure history.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Indeed. That is also part of the issues you've got to address.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: Your Honours, this photograph was first disclosed via CD-ROM on the 9th of March, 2007. Subsequently, it was re-disclosed each time the Prosecution disclosed its 65 ter exhibit list in toto to the Defence. And on those occasions it was disclosed on an external hard drive. That occurred on the 2nd of May, 2008; and then, again, on the 7th of May, 2008; and then when there was a change of Defence counsel in the summer of 2008, it was disclosed again on the 16th of June, 2008 to the present Defence counsel. That is the disclosure history, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: And why was it not used in evidence in-chief?

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: It is my understanding, Your Honour, that it wasn't necessary, given the fact that there were agreed facts pertaining to the events in Srebrenica. It was considered not to be necessary, given the agreed facts pertaining to Srebrenica.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: And what was the fact that was agreed specifically?

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: The fact, Your Honour, was the following: It's fact number 26. This is now from the second decision in respect of the Srebrenica agreed facts, 30th of September, 2009. On the 16th of July, 1995, Kozluk on 15 or 16 July 1995, VRS and/or MUP soldiers transported about 500 Bosnian Muslim males to an isolated place near Kozluk and summarily executed them with automatic weapons. These Bosnian Muslim men had been captured from the column of men retreating from the Srebrenica enclave, or separated in Potocari. On the 16th of July, 1995, VRS soldiers buried the victims of the executions in a mass grave thereby.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: All those facts, it is not one fact. All those facts that are you mentioning do not touch upon heightened security along the border. So this is a completely different topic.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: Well, Your Honour, the heightened security - yeah - referred to by this witness is pertaining obviously to these -- to these facts that I have just read.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Mr. Saxon, this witness comes from Serbia. He is talking by heightened security by the Serb forces on the border.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: That's right.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: The facts that are you talking about have to do with the VRS, the capture of the Muslims, and taking them to wherever they were killed, and the killing of those Muslims. Where is the reference, where is the agreed fact on the security on the border?

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: Your point is taken, Your Honour. There is no agreed fact on the security along the border.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Right.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: But, if I may, Your Honour, you asked me why this photograph was not used.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: And quite frankly, a great deal of what we referred to then as crime base evidence, decisions were made not to use it, based on the facts -- based -- based on the reality that we had agreed facts related to Srebrenica.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: I -- I don't dispute that you had the agreed facts related to Srebrenica, sir.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: All I'm saying is, from the facts that you have recited, the fact of heightened security along the border is not mentioned.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: You're right.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: And I do not see then how evidence about a crime base can be used to contradict testimony about heighten security along the border.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: Well --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: I don't see how you connect these two.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: Your Honour, the -- this particular photograph, if I'm given leave to use it, will be used to test the -- what the witness said regarding to supposed measures of heightened security because what it shows -- what this photograph shows is the proximity of, if you will, the crime base of the Kozluk killing site to Serbia. That is what this photograph shows.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Right. And let me find out. This murder area, this crime base area, is it on the Serb side or the RS side?

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: It is on the RS side, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Yes. And then -- and where was it where the Serb's border security is? On the Serb side.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour, it does.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Now, what -- of what interest from the point of view of border security would an activity taking place on the other side of the river in another country got to do with the question of security?

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: Well, if you will, it goes to the failure of the border security patrols to report what was going on, Your Honour. And this is important. I'm going to go back to the witness's testimony right now. Because if you look at what the witness said, this is at the top of page -- the bottom of page 10094 where Mr. Lukic and the witness were discussing an unsuccessful attempt by members of the 28th Division of the Muslim Army to break through to Tuzla during the events around Srebrenica. At line 22 Mr. Lukic asked: "General, for you at the operations centre was the movement of the 28th Division of the Muslim Army an important military movement at the time." The answer: "Yes." And then Mr. Lukic asked why. And at the top of page 10095, the witness said with respect to the fact that Srebrenica is near the border with the FRY: "It is near the border with the FRY, and these forces that I described here during their withdrawal and during their attempted breakthrough, part of them could have headed across the border towards the FRY."

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Mm-hm.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: "Therefore, it was important to take measures of heightened security."

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: I understand that perfectly well. I still don't understand why you expect Serb security border officer to report - I don't know to whom - what happens in another country.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: Well, Your Honour, if you take a look at D227, and this Trial Chamber admitted this document just, I believe it was on Thursday afternoon, it's a document from the daily operations report of the operations centre of the VJ General Staff, and it is reporting about -- it is reporting about -- information about persons who had crossed over from Srebrenica and, Your Honour, it is --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Crossed over into Serbia.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: Crossed over into Serbia, yes, and it also reports that according to a wounded prisoner, about 20 to 30 Muslims, men and women, were waiting in the Kozluk village sector that is in Republika Srpska, just across the river. And that they would try to enter the Federal Republic of Yugoslavia after night-fall.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: But according to your wounded prisoner -- okay, I hear what you say. Are you done?

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: I believe so, Your Honour. I do want to explore with the witness the failure of reporting about the events at Kozluk.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: I thought you wanted to explore with the witness security measures along the border.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: Well, yes, Your Honour, but that -- I'm sorry if I'm misspeaking, but security measures at least from the Prosecution's perspective, would include whether they were monitoring what was going on at Kozluk because they were just -- they were apparently warned that people were going to try to cross over that evening and whether they were reporting what happened at Kozluk. It is all part, Your Honour, of what we look at is border security. It's monitoring, but it is also reporting up.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Mr. Lukic or Mr. Guy-Smith.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: As I submitted, I don't believe that Mr. Saxon has made any compelling argument with regard to the issue that he has presented.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: The Chamber [Microphone not activated] The Chamber by majority, Judge Moloto dissenting, grants your application.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honours. Can the witness be --

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: Before the witness comes in, if that's the Chamber's ruling, considering that Mr. Saxon has testified with regard to what the photograph is, I trust that Mr. Saxon is not going to tell the witness what the photograph is when he is questioning him but in the first instance is going to determine whether or not the witness recognises the photograph or not, because if the witness recognises the photograph that might lead to one level of examination. If the witness does not recognise the photograph, that would end this particular discussion. Since the photograph is being used as a basis for impeachment, it would require, of course, if the witness was being cross-examined in some fashion either recognises the document, the subject matter, or is in a position to accept something with regard to the representation made in the document. Since we're dealing with an image here, I think it is relatively important since the sole reason of this particular tendering is to impeach the witness with regard to a specific issue, it is important to make a determination of whether or not the witness, in fact, recognises the image that he is being shown.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Can I suggest that -- I'm sorry, Mr. Saxon. I guess, Mr. Saxon heard your warning, but I still suppose that Mr. Saxon has the liberty to conduct his cross-examination the way he wants. I urge you, if he does anything that you think is objectionable to stand up at that time and object. We can't deal with an objection in anticipation or on speculation.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: Understood, and I thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: You're welcome.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: If I just may ask one question of Defence counsel. Is it the position of the Defence that this photograph does not depict the Kozluk execution site?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: That's what I was trying to avoid. Now you're going into dialogue. Answer, Mr. Guy-Smith.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: We were, I think, previously asked to stipulate to this photograph which we declined because we don't know.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: Can we call in the witness, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: The witness may be called in.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] While we're waiting for the witness to be taken into the courtroom, I would like to intervene into the transcript, page 11, line 2. It wasn't Witness Nikola Koljevic who was mentioned, rather, Witness Simic.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Saxon, are you able to help? Oh, yes, witness Simic should be -- thank you. Thank you, Mr. Lukic.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: We thank you once again for your consideration, Mr. Simic, and apologise for the inconvenience we're causing you. Mr. Saxon.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: Good afternoon, General Simic.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Microphone, please.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Microphone, Mr. Saxon.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: Good afternoon, General Simic.

utterances.speaker: MIODRAG SIMIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Good afternoon, Mr. Prosecutor.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: I'd like to take you back, please, to your testimony on Thursday when you were discussing an intelligence report with Mr. Lukic. This was at page 10094 of the transcript. And this particular intelligence report from the 2nd Administration was dated the 13th of July, 1995, and it discussed the events that were then occurring around Srebrenica. And the report described an unsuccessful attempt by members of the 28th Division of the Muslim Army to breakthrough towards Kladanj and Tuzla. And at line 22, Mr. Lukic asked you this: "General, for you at the operations centre, was the movement of the 28th Division of the Muslim Army an important military movement at the time?" And you answered: "Yes." And then Mr. Lukic asked you why. And at the top of page 10095 of the transcript, you explained that Srebrenica is near the border with the Federal Republic of Yugoslavia. "And these forces that I described here during their withdrawal and during their attempted breakthrough, part of them could have headed across the border towards the FRY?" And you continued: "Therefore, it was important to take measures of heightened security along the state border so that such armed persons would not cross the border or, rather, even if they were to cross the border, that we act in accordance with the border service rules." Do you recall that testimony?

utterances.speaker: MIODRAG SIMIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I recall it fully, Mr. Prosecutor.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: Very well.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: And if we can, please, show the witness D227. And I have a copy in Serbo-Croat, which if this could be shown to Mr. Lukic or Mr. Gregor Guy-Smith before giving it to the witness, I'd be grateful. And perhaps we could increase the size of the font on the English side, it's quite small.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: General Simic, this was a daily operations report that Mr. Lukic showed to you last week. It's from your former administration, from the operations centre. It's dated 16th July, 1995, and we see this report is from 0600 on the 15th of July to 0600 on the 16th of July, 1995.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: Can we scroll down in both languages, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: And we see on the bottom of the first page, we see a subtitle, number 2: Situation at the state border.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: Could we now turn to the following page, please, in both languages.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: And, General Simic, if you just focus, please, at the top paragraph on that second page. It tells us this: "At around 1600 hours on 15 July, a civilian called Petrovic from Gornja Koviljaca village at elevation Trbusnica, 15th Loznica border battalion said that a wounded Muslim soldier (earlier acquaintance) called Resid Simonevic was staying at his place and was seeking medical attention. Petrovic said that this man was from Bratunac but the doctor at the Banja Koviljaca medical centre recognised him as being from Srebrenica. Petrovic said that two other Muslim soldiers were having lunch in Banja Koviljaca and had taken the bus to go to Mali Zvornik." And these communities Banja Koviljaca, Mali Zvornik, those are on the FRY side of the Drina River; isn't that right?

utterances.speaker: MIODRAG SIMIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: Then it continues: "Resid, the wounded man, said that about 20 to 30 Muslims (men and women) were waiting in the Kozluk village sector and that they would try to enter the FRY after night-fall." And now the Kozluk village sector was on the Republika Srpska side of the Drina river, right?

utterances.speaker: MIODRAG SIMIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: Sir, if we just stop here for a moment, this information provided by a captured Muslim man was important enough to send from the VJ border unit up the VJ chain of command and to be included in the daily OPs report of the 1st Administration of the VJ General Staff. Correct?

utterances.speaker: MIODRAG SIMIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Not the 1st Administration of the army's General Staff, rather, the operations centre of the VJ Main Staff. Now, the fact that the operations centre falls within the 1st Administration is a different matter. It is of service to the chief of the General Staff and the General Staff in general, in collecting, assessing, and processing information.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: All right. And so the answer to my question, though, would be a yes, wouldn't it? This information about the wounded man and that 20 to 30 Muslims who were waiting in Kozluk to enter the FRY after night-fall was important enough to be included in the daily report of the operations centre. That's what we see here. Right?

utterances.speaker: MIODRAG SIMIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's what the assessment of the duty officers was at the time. That it was relevant, and that's why it was included in the operative report. And I said that the shift included two officers and one being the superior, and they had the rank of a colonel, and they would be the ones assessing information.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: All right. General, in light of the measures of heightened security along the state border that you described earlier in your testimony, starting on the afternoon of the 15th of July, 1995, the VJ border units in the Drina river valley would have focussed more attention on the area of Kozluk village, on the other side of the Drina river, wouldn't they?

utterances.speaker: MIODRAG SIMIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. Heightened security along the length of the border with Republika Srpska was in place. However, there was no special attention being attached to these very individuals crossing the border. Rather, there were certain sections where people were expected to cross the border. Patrols were dispatched or ambushes set. We wouldn't send a unit from the depth of the territory in order to take up positions along the border. I think that we are viewing the matter somewhat differently.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: Well, let me follow along, if I can, on -- on -- follow along your response. You said that there were certain sections where people were expected to cross the border. And so at 1600 hours on the 15th of July, the VJ border unit was informed that in the area of Kozluk village in Republika Srpska, there was a group of Muslims who would try to cross the border after night-fall. And so wouldn't some attention have been paid to that area of the border, across from Kozluk village, if there was "heightened security," to use your term?

utterances.speaker: MIODRAG SIMIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Mr. Prosecutor, let us clarify a methodological matter. It is up to the source of the information, and this was taken over from intelligence sources. The information reached us in the evening. Now, was the information immediately conveyed to the border units or not is a different matter. We took the information from the report we received in the evening which was normally analysed at 2100 hours, and this was on the 15th. But in -- independently of this report, we had heightened our security along the length of the border with the Republika Srpska. We've already explained what heightened security meant. We did not deploy units along the length of the border. It was merely at certain sections of the border. I don't recall the dates now, but we have seen these reports. Heightened security was exercised by the border units themselves at various points. I said that there was a border belt which was 100 metres deep. It takes an infantry soldier to run the distance in a minute or two. Beyond the 100-metre belt we have restricted powers in terms of intervening, and that's why the ambushes are set within the border belt and not beyond.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: General, according to --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Lukic.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Rather, page 17, line 5 it says "an infantry soldier," whereas the witness used the term "pedestrian."

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: And are you able to help us, Mr. Lukic, or even the witness, with the last word on that same line, distance in a ... In a minute. Okay. Yeah. As I understand, he said: "In a minute or two." One minute or two. That's what I heard the interpretation go.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: That's correct, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Thank you very much, Madam Interpreter. Yes, Mr. Saxon.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: You see, General Simic, at least in the English version of this document at the top of page 2 we're told that the 15th Loznica border battalion received this information. And so what I'm trying to explore with you is if a border battalion near the Drina river at that time was informed that there was a group of Muslims who planned to cross the river at a particular area they were at a level -- the border battalion was at a level of heightened security, wouldn't that border battalion or a piece of it, focus some of its attention on that part of the river?

utterances.speaker: MIODRAG SIMIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: You can see from the text, sir, that that border battalion and the soldier told them how he came there and that they knew. But on a case to case basis we don't issue an order for us to be running from the General Staff and issue commands. Their general task was to secure the border in that sector. So there are no more interventions by the General Staff or the army command. There's no need again to place line of soldiers preventing people from crossing over. If there's civilians, I mean, they will cross over, they will violate the border regime, they will be caught, handed over to the MUP organs, and handed on for further processing, and that is where the authority of the army ends. That is all that I can say about that.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: Mr. Simic, I didn't ask you if this required an additional intervention by the General Staff or the Army Command. I simply asked you if the border battalion was on, what you referred to as "heightened security measures." Then given this information, logically, the border battalion might have focussed some of its attention on the Kozluk section of this --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Mr. Guy-Smith.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: This is the third time Mr. Saxon has asked the question. I think at this point it is appropriate to intervene and say asked and answered as an objection.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: It has not been answered, Your Honour, I'm sorry. My question has not been answered.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Question allowed.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: Can you answer my question, General?

utterances.speaker: MIODRAG SIMIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Sir, if the General Staff were to deal with ad hoc events from hour to hour this would be endless. They received the order for heightened security measures at the state border. It's a question of the battalion or -- or company, or the garrison commander which organs he would send where for those purposes. This is something that the General Staff would not be involved in further. So I don't really know how else to answer this question.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: If I may, Your Honour. I believe that Mr. Saxon is mistaken. He may not have gotten the answer that he wanted, but he certainly asked the question and received an answer. He asked the question beginning at line -- page 15, line 19 and more specifically he said referring to line 22 -- 21: "The VJ border units in the Drina river valley would have focussed more attention on the area of Kozluk village, on the other side of the Drina river, wouldn't they? "A. No. Heightened security along the length of the border with Republika Srpska was in place." And then the witness goes on. So he has received an answer to the question. It may not be the answer that he wishes. But he has received an answer.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: Well, the thing is, Your Honour, I then asked a follow-up question based on the answer of the witness. And that's at page 16, starting at line 6. And then I got a response, a lengthy response, regarding methodology that did not answer my question. And that's where we are now. And I still have not received an answer to my question. But I will move on, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: [Microphone not activated] "... at 1600 hours on the 15th of July, the VJ border unit was informed that in the area of Kozluk village in Republika Srpska, there was a group of Muslims who would try to cross the border after night-fall. And so wouldn't some attention have been paid to that area of the border, across the Kozluk village, if there was 'heightened security,' to use your term?" Now, my first problem with that question is that it is speculative; it is not factual. And it can only be answered by people who were along the border, if you must get a factual answer. But I'm not going into that. That is not the basis of the objection.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: Your Honour, I have heard the objection, I've heard Your Honour and I'm going to move on.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Saxon.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: In this case, General Simic, General Perisic has agreed that: "On the 15th or 16th of July, 1995, VRS or MUP -- and/or MUP soldiers transported about 500 Bosnian Muslim males to an isolated place near Kozluk and summarily executed them with automatic weapons. These Bosnian Muslim men had been captured from the column of men retreating from the Srebrenica enclave or separated in Potocari. "On the 16th July, 1995, VRS soldiers buried the victims of the executions in a mass grave nearby." That has been agreed to by the parties in this case. Do you know, sir, if and when VJ units reported this massacre of 500 Bosnian Muslim males that occurred near the village of Kozluk on the 15th or 16th July?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Lukic.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I think that this question has not put fairly and that the witness should have been told that the agreement was made based on agreed facts.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: You see, that's my problem, Mr. Saxon. You've told the witness that this is an agreed fact, and then your question then says, does he know when the VJ units reported. They're not saying they saw. They say they are agreeing to the fact that it has been proposed. Look at -- look at your question at page 21, line -- starting from line 4. You are suggesting that the VJ units knew -- either somehow knew about it or observed it and therefore reported it.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: Well, I will rephrase the question, and I will ask him if he is aware whether VJ units learned of this.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: General Simic, are you aware whether VJ units became aware of this execution of 500 Bosnian Muslims outside of Kozluk?

utterances.speaker: MIODRAG SIMIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I can confirm that I learned about it if you showed me a report by my official organs where the General Staff officially informed about that. I -- until I see that, I really cannot confirm it, and I don't know where these facts come from. I'm responsible for -- for the soldiers, for the border security. If that was something that they did, then I probably would have had to have known about it. But I would like to see the report on it indicating when this was established.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: And in your memory, do you have any knowledge or recollection of receiving such a report?

utterances.speaker: MIODRAG SIMIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I do not have any recollection of that, no.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: Can we please show the witness, I believe we have an extra copy of the photograph, 65 ter 4310.02. And if we can call that up on the ELMO, please. If the usher could assist, please. I'm sorry, I meant to say e-court, not on the ELMO.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: General Simic, are you familiar at all with the Kozluk area?

utterances.speaker: MIODRAG SIMIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: Do you recognise any part of this photograph on the upper left-hand side?

utterances.speaker: MIODRAG SIMIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I recognise the terrain the river is flowing through. And then in the upper right-hand corner you can see the outline of a settlement, but I really cannot be sure of that.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: I will withdraw this photograph now. I'm going to move now to another topic. Actually, no, before I move on --

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: Automatic weapons fire used to shoot 500 individuals, that makes a lot of noise, doesn't it, General?

utterances.speaker: MIODRAG SIMIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: If you have in mind that there was combat in that area and that a breakthrough was attempted, who, among the border guards could have assumed that something was happening there. I don't know if that's what you're aiming at. That or combat that is legal in terms of military regulations. I mean, really, I cannot answer this we with the proviso that they probably did hear. I mean, not probably but had to have heard. But a soldier on the border in a forest on guard is unable to conclude what is happening, and we have to place ourselves in a real situation in the area where this was actually happening not as if we were looking at it now and saying, well, here this is what's happening over there, or this is what happened over there.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: And soldiers in a forest who hear a lot of firing report that, or they're supposed to, aren't they, particularly if they're at a level of heightened security?

utterances.speaker: MIODRAG SIMIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Sir, you're absolutely correct. They were there, entrenched in the forest, watching, observing. Perhaps they had binoculars. Often they didn't have binoculars along the border. The border had just been established. There were no border posts. The border-line was not defined. It was an improvised thing still. So whatever they were able to hear would be something that they would also report. There was shooting on a daily basis, so he couldn't really determine what was going on with that firing or fire today or yesterday. As far as he is concerned, it would be shooting between two armies.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: I'm going to move on.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: Can we show the witness what is Exhibit D224, please. And I've got a copy to show to counsel before it is given to the witness. And if we could increase the size of the English, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: General Simic, on Thursday, Mr. Lukic showed you this document. It's a report from the 2nd Administration of the Army of Republika Srpska -- excuse me, it's a report from the 2nd Administration of the sector for operations and staff affairs of the VJ General Staff dated the 14th of July, 1995. And at pages 10097 to 10099 on Thursday, you confirmed to Mr. Lukic that the information about the VRS offensive against Zepa was important enough to enter into the report of the duty OPs centre of the VJ General Staff.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: Can we scroll down in both languages, please, and focus on the last paragraph for those following in English, where it says: "In the Zepa enclave, the Muslim Army rejected a VRS request for peaceful demilitarization. After the expiry of the deadline for compliance with the request, at 1100 hours, the VRS launched an attack on the Zepa enclave in order to take it and put it under VRS control." Are you following me?

utterances.speaker: MIODRAG SIMIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Absolutely, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: If this information about the VRS attack on the Zepa enclave was important enough to enter into the daily report of the duty OPs centre, then, logically, the VRS offensive against the Srebrenica enclave that began in July 1995 would also have been at least reported to the duty OPs centre. Don't you agree?

utterances.speaker: MIODRAG SIMIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I would have to look at the daily combat report of the 15th, whether it was entered or not. But, again, I'm saying that it's a question of the person processing the daily operations report. This is a report by the intelligence administration. They meet at 2100 hours at the operations centre. They analyse all the information that arrives, and then they make the decision about what is important to be noted in the daily operations report for the chief of the General Staff. I can only tell you now that, in any case, it's both yes and no. It's important and it's not important. Why important? Because it is happening near the border and could, during combat, result in a number of armed people from the other side crossing the border. It's not important from the aspect of the fact that we have already taken adequate measures in respect of the border. To be more explicit, I cannot really say yes or no until I look at the daily operations report.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: I'm going to stop there, General Lukic [sic]. Thank you very much for your time and for your patience.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: And, Your Honour, those are all the questions that I have.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Saxon. Mr. Lukic, any re-examination?

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] General Simic, once more, good afternoon.

utterances.speaker: MIODRAG SIMIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Good afternoon, Mr. Lukic.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Well, I just want to tell you that we will not be spending much more time in this courtroom. You would be able to move out and go back to your home, to your family soon. I'm going to go back to the Drina Plan to what Mr. Saxon spent most of his time discussing with you. Mr. Saxon showed you a document yesterday.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Can we please look at document 1562 on the screen, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Mr. Simic, I don't have a -- hard copies of those documents, but I think we are going to go through them very quickly. You would be able to see it on the screen. Maybe during the break we will be able to do something.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] This is a P exhibit, 1562. We'll wait a little bit.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Let me see if I do have a hard copy for you.

utterances.speaker: MIODRAG SIMIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, I've already seen the document, so it's clear to me.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: This document was shown to you by Mr. Saxon yesterday when you were looking at the documents of the 1st Krajina Corps relating to the Drina Plan, and I'm going add, of the Army of the Republika Srpska. I'm interested in the following.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Can we scroll the document up a little bit, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Mr. Saxon showed this to you. And can you see the signatures at the bottom. On the left-hand side, we have something that I am unable to read. It says "submitted by" and then there's the signature of the person. Actually, let us look at the right-hand corner of the document first to see who received it. Can you read who received the list?

utterances.speaker: MIODRAG SIMIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: In my copy it says Miletic.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: You've already replied to Saxon that Mr. Miletic was the main operative in the Main Staff of the Army of Republika Srpska, your counterpart in the General Staff of the 1st Administration of the VJ. Does this document show that the documents of the 1st Krajina Corps representing the excerpts of the VRS plan are returned to the Main Staff of the Army of Republika Srpska?

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: Objection. This's a leading question.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I think that I did not, because it says: "Received by and submitted by." Your Honours, I was just, I think that I just ...

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: [Previous translation continues] ... the form of your question is still leading.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Very well. I apologise.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: General, will you please tell us, what does this document say?

utterances.speaker: MIODRAG SIMIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I've said this before, and I'm repeating this again using this particular example. The command of the 1st Krajina Corps thus received an excerpt from the plan on the use of the Main Staff of the Army of Republika Srpska which relates to the 1st Krajina Corps. Once the command of the 1st Krajina Corps developed its documents, it sent a copy for keeping to the Main Staff, and that is precisely this list of documents of the 1st Krajina Corps submitted to the General Staff of the Army of Republika Srpska. I asserted the whole time that all levels of command develop plans of use in two copies. One remains at the command, the unit implementing the assignment, and the other copy is sent to the superior command, and you can see that very clearly here.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Is this the proper procedure which should be followed, that is, that excerpts are sent to the subordinate command, and a copy is submitted to the superior command?

utterances.speaker: MIODRAG SIMIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that is the correct methodology.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: General, are you familiar whether the Drina Corps signed by Mr. Lilic - this is P215 - were excerpts done for that plan which were submitted to the subordinate units?

utterances.speaker: MIODRAG SIMIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Did you see a copy of a report or excerpts like this of the subordinate unit which was returned to the person who actually drafted the directive?

utterances.speaker: MIODRAG SIMIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: May I interrupt you a little bit, Mr. Lukic. Page 28, line 11, I think you said: "Are you familiar with the Drina Corps plan signed by Mr. Lilic."

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, I see the error. I see the error. I correct myself. It's not the Drina Corps.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: [Previous translation continues] ...

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I was thinking of the Drina Plan signed by Mr. Lilic. So the word "corps" is not necessary here, we're talking about the Drina Plan. The Drina Plan is referred to very frequently. So I'm going be referring to it in terms of P215, and I'm also going to call it the directive on the use of the Army of Yugoslavia, the Army of Republika Srpska, and the Serbian Army of the Krajina signed by Mr. Lilic, and I'm going to repeat my question to be precise.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Have you ever seen any kind of excerpt returned by any of the subordinate units to the body that drafted the plan in the General Staff? This is what I'm asking you.

utterances.speaker: MIODRAG SIMIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Mr. Lukic, nobody was able to send excerpts unless they had previously been given the entire plan by Mr. Lilic. I said at the outset that the directive is one of the integral parts of the plan, but on its own it doesn't mean anything.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Had an excerpt been sent to a subordinate unit, the list as we see it now on our screen, would have to have been returned to Mr. Lilic.

utterances.speaker: MIODRAG SIMIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. The list that I'm holding in my hands right now which relates to the 1st Krajina Corps, it's on the basis of this that both Main Staffs would have had to produce their own plan of use and would have had to send this back to Mr. Lilic.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Can we have our break now, Your Honours?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Indeed, we can and we may. We will come back at 4.00. Court adjourned.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Mr. Lukic.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] General, we have got hold of a hard copy.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Can we go back to P215, which is directive on the use of the Army of Yugoslavia, the Army of Republika Srpska, and the Serbian Army of the Krajina.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Could we have page 1 shown of this document, which you discussed with Mr. Saxon.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Could we, in fact, turn to page 17 of both the B/C/S and English versions.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: General, this is the page marked 16 in your copy, and that's the page where we have Mr. Lilic's signature. Following Roman numeral VI where you have the heading, what follows under VII are annexes. They cover various fields of activity. Under III, we have intelligence situation. Under IV, we have the intelligence plan.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Could we now turn to page 21 of the B/C/S version, and that's page 37 of the English version. I seem to have mentioned the wrong number. Give me a moment, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] There it is. And the B/C/S. Could we have the same page in the B/C/S, the one that we're looking at right now.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: General, this is about the intelligence situation, Annex number 3. Could you please try and find it in your copy.

utterances.speaker: MIODRAG SIMIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I have.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: We don't have the appropriate B/C/S page, but it will follow shortly, I think. A moment ago, under Annexes I read under III, intelligence situation. Can you tell us in the upper right-hand corner what is it stated? What sort of annex is this?

utterances.speaker: MIODRAG SIMIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Mr. Lukic, in the upper right-hand corner, we have National Defence, state secret, Drina, annex number 3, copy number 1.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Is that Annex 3 referred to in the earlier page, which was page 17?

utterances.speaker: MIODRAG SIMIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Can we now skip several pages and look at Annex 4. That's page 38 of the B/C/S and 48 of the English version, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Annexes 3 and 4, were they signed by anyone?

utterances.speaker: MIODRAG SIMIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: On page 4 of Annex 4, one can see that it's states that the chief of the Yugoslav Army for the SVK and the VRS as well. We have the signature lines in place, but nobody's signed there.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: What does this tell you, General?

utterances.speaker: MIODRAG SIMIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: It tells me that the plan on the use of forces was not fully complete, and, therefore, not fully valid.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Thank you. We will not be using e-court. Rather, we will be using page 16 where all the various annexes were listed, General. You can see under 11, it is stated: "Security support."

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Perhaps for your benefit, Your Honour, that is page 17 of the B/C/S and page 17 of the English.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Under 11 it says: "Security support."

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: [Previous translation continues] ... security support or intelligence support, under 11?

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, I think that the translation is wrong, because what it says is "security support." You've observed it rightly because what -- what we have is intelligence support plan is under 4.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: So this is what we under 11, General.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Could we now turn to the page where we have Annex 11, which is in the B/C/S version, 63, and in the English, 82.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: For your benefit, General, that's heading: Security support. And will you see it says Annex 11. I don't know if you can follow.

utterances.speaker: MIODRAG SIMIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I have found it.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: What can you read in the upper right-hand corner, General?

utterances.speaker: MIODRAG SIMIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Mr. Lukic, as with the earlier annex, it states: National Defence, state secret, R, Drina, annex number 11, copy number 1.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Is that Annex 11 referred to in the list of annexes?

utterances.speaker: MIODRAG SIMIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Let us skip four pages ahead, since what is to follow is the plan of security measures.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] We will be looking at page 3, that's right; and in the English version, that's page 85, I think, Your Honours. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: What do we see on this page, General?

utterances.speaker: MIODRAG SIMIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: On page 3 of Annex 11, we can see two columns. The left-hand column reads: "Drafted by." And then below the line, we have for the Army of Yugoslavia, Hristivoje Jocic; still below for the Serbian Army of Krajina, Vuk Dmitrovic; for the Army of Republika Srpska, Jovica Karanovic, and typed up by Marica Pavlovic. We don't see their signatures though. In the column on the right-hand side, it is written for the Army of Yugoslavia for the Army of Republika Srpska for the Serbian Army of the Krajina. Chiefs of security administrations of the respective armies were supposed to sign there.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Is this a valid document, as it stands now, without any signatures, and can it be acted upon as such?

utterances.speaker: MIODRAG SIMIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: In order for this document to be implemented, can anyone be given an excerpt of this document or be asked to return a copy as a follow-up of the excerpt if there are no signatures here?

utterances.speaker: MIODRAG SIMIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] This is yet another annex, Your Honour. We will have to be moving into private session.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: May the Chamber please move into private session. No, don't.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Apologies, truly.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: [Microphone not activated]

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: At page 17, let us look at Annex number 10 which is entitled: Logistics support.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Can we turn to page 54 of the B/C/S version in e-court and page 70 of the English version.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: General, I don't know if you're following me.

utterances.speaker: MIODRAG SIMIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: What can you read in the upper right-hand corner?

utterances.speaker: MIODRAG SIMIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: National Defence of People's Defence, state secret, R, Drina, annex number 10, copy number 1.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Look at the annex and the extent of pages that it has, and can you tell us has it been signed by anyone?

utterances.speaker: MIODRAG SIMIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] There is a document I would like to show to the witness as a follow-up on what the Prosecutor asked the witness about the Drina Plan. We received the document from the OTP as part of their disclosures in the past couple of days. The only thing I'm not certain about is whether the document is confidential or not, whether there are any protective measures. Perhaps we should move into private session so that I can verify this with the OTP. I have just been told that they were informed that the document did not have any protective measures. This is document marked by the OTP as XN-100. Since it's a rather large document, it is page 81 of the B/C/S version. There is no English translation of the document, and I have produced several copies of a draft translation for your benefit, Your Honours, and for the Prosecution. I will also have a copy for Mr. Simic. Page 81.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: When, during your examination-in-chief, Mr. Simic -- or, rather, let me give you some time to look at the document.

utterances.speaker: MIODRAG SIMIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I produced the document.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: This is my question for you. During your examination-in-chief, you explained to us that the -- a separate certification needs to be compiled by all those taking part in producing the document. Or let me just correct the interpretation. The witness said I am quite clear on the document. That's page 35, line 9. He didn't say that he produced the document. As we can see, this is a document of the Serbian Army of the Krajina from a different period all together, the 17th of February, 1995. What I'm interested in is the format, General. Judging by its format, what sort of document would you say this is?

utterances.speaker: MIODRAG SIMIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: This is a statement.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: [Previous translation continues] ... Mr. Saxon.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: If the transcript in English that I'm reading is correct at page 35 line 12, this appears to be a question arising out of examination-in-chief. And is that a mistranslation or a --

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] No. Let me just clarify this. During the examination-in-chief, I asked the General -- or, rather, the General himself was explaining what was involved in the production of the directive. Now, what I'm asking has to do about the cross-examination conducted by Mr. Saxon and in relation to the issue of whether the Drina Plan directive was properly produced, and this was something that was extensively discussed by Mr. Saxon. So I want to ask the witness, in relation to this document --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: [Previous translation continues] ... so you want to correct -- what line was it, Mr. Saxon?

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: Line 12.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Line 12.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: Page 35.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Now, yes. Do you want to correct the word "examination-in-chief" in line 12 to "cross-examination?" Is that what are you saying?

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] No. I did state this correctly. However, the question I wish to put to the witness relates to the line of questioning arising from Mr. Saxon's cross-examination. And this --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: [Previous translation continues] ... cross-examination, not to your questions in-chief?

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: And if I may, Your Honour, certainly this document was not used during cross-examination by the Prosecution.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] We got this document. I saw it for the first time, perhaps we got it a couple of days before the examination began of Mr. Simic by the Prosecution. This is the entire set of documents that we received at the time when I had already completed the proofing notes. This is number one. But this is not my reason. It's possible that we received the documents a few days before that. This is that big disclosure we received. It's correct that the document was not used in the cross-examination, since Mr. Saxon put a whole line of questions about the procedure, how the Army of Republika Srpska drafted its Drina Plan. That is why I would like to put this question to the witness, whether this document is part of the procedure as it is usually followed when such a plan is drafted, and whether he, while he was doing his work, did something like this or, rather, signed it. The whole line of Mr. Saxon refers to that. The four sessions of the hearing boiled down to showing documents about what the Army of Republika Srpska did as far as the implementation of the directives is concerned. I think this directly arises from the cross-examination by Mr. Saxon.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Saxon.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: Well, if that -- if the purpose of Mr. Lukic's re-direct examination is to counter the points or arguments that I made with the documents that I showed the witness during cross-examination, Prosecution believes the proper way to do that is with those same documents.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I think that I am not obliged to follow the documents of the Prosecution in my re-direct but the topics of the Prosecution.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Mr. Saxon, let me ask you a question. To the extent that the Prosecution is allowed to use documents in cross-examination after resting its case that were not used in examination-in-chief, is the Defence not accorded the same right or privilege where it uses the same -- similar -- other documents also for the purpose of either buttressing what they have said or contradicting what the Prosecution position is?

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: If -- Your Honour, if the particular document will buttress their position or contradict the Prosecution position from those new documents, then I will concede Your Honours' point, yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Thank you. You may proceed, Mr. Lukic. If that is the purpose, the purpose is to buttress your position or to contradict the -- the contradiction by the Prosecution?

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Sir, what does this document talk about?

utterances.speaker: MIODRAG SIMIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: This is a strictly formalised document speaking about the statement given by the person that is participating in the drafting of the plan of usage. That is that solemn declaration in the army that a person is working on the plan of usage and that they would respect and keep state secrets.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Are you aware that you or anybody else who worked on the Drina Plan that I am going to refer to as P215 to be precise, signed such a statement, and did they submit it to anyone?

utterances.speaker: MIODRAG SIMIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I would like to tender this document, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: Your Honour, if the Chamber is minded to admit this document, we would ask that it be admitted marked for identification, since we do not yet have an English translation.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Indeed, Mr. Lukic indicated that this is just a draft translation by himself. Okay. The document is admitted into evidence, marked for identification. May it please be given an exhibit number.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honours. This document shall be assigned Exhibit Number D238, marked for identification. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: General, while you were at the post you were at in the 1st Administration in the General Staff sector of the Army of Yugoslavia, did you hear or were you informed by anyone that the Army of Republika Srpska developed or made its Drina Plan, adopted the Drina Plan?

utterances.speaker: MIODRAG SIMIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: First of all, I would have to know about it because, at the same time, at the head of the organisational units where all of these plans are kept, in view of the fact that President Lilic signed the directive, and if the plans were to come from the Main Staffs of both armies, since he does not have his own premises, the General Staff of the Army of Yugoslavia, as his service, would naturally be kept -- those plans would naturally be kept just like any other plans are kept. So I would have to know about that plan in the same way that I would have to know about all the other plans that are being kept there.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: General, since you were informed about the preparation of the directives and you were informed about it, did anybody show you or perhaps were you shown earlier any document of the Army of the Serbian Army of Krajina that referred to any aspect of the Drina Plan?

utterances.speaker: MIODRAG SIMIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: For a moment, can we --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Just a second. The interpreter said Serbian Army of Krajina relating to the Drina Plan.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] That's correct, yes. That was my question.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: [Previous translation continues] ...

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] We already looked at the VRS so my question now is ...

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: [Previous translation continues]... thank you. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Can we move to private session for a moment, please?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: May the Chamber please move into private session.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: We're in private session, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Thank you, sir. Yes, Mr. Lukic.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I don't know if we would need to move to closed session, just because of the possibility that the document would be broadcast outside. I would like to us look at the document on the screen, but I would not wish to have the document broadcast outside. We're talking about P1564.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Can you guide us, Mr. Registrar. Does closed session make sure that the document is -- May we move into closed session then.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: I'm told it is okay with private session. You said it is P1564?

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: That's right. That's right.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Perhaps we should have looked, General, in order to avoid confusion, at P215. We don't have to put it on the screen, but you will confirm this for me. These are the attachments that go with the Drina Plan.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Can we see what goes under number 5.

utterances.speaker: MIODRAG SIMIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: 5 is the communications plan.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: That is correct. This document that we have in front of us, can you please tell us what the heading says?

utterances.speaker: MIODRAG SIMIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: It says: People's Defence, state secret, Drina, copy number 1, supplement or attachment number 5.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Is that supposed to be the attachment that accompanies P215, except we have a different number?

utterances.speaker: MIODRAG SIMIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Can you please turn to page 2 now.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Can we look at the B/C/S and English versions on the screen.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: What does this document tell you, General?

utterances.speaker: MIODRAG SIMIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: This is a list of documents comprising this communications plan. This is a list of the documents. It's headed: List of documents of the communications plan.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Is this a valid document? Was it submitted to anyone? Did anybody receive this document? Look at the bottom of the page.

utterances.speaker: MIODRAG SIMIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: There is no person listed as submitting it or receiving it, and there is to distribution list either on this document.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: This document, without such data, can that go into distribution?

utterances.speaker: MIODRAG SIMIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No document without a signature can be valid for further distribution.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Let us go back to open session, please, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: May the Chamber please move into open session.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: We're back in open session, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Thank you so much. Yes, Mr. Lukic.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Another question on the same topic. Can we show the witness D155, please. It's P1555, three 5s. Yes, right -- good.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: You've looked at this document already with Mr. Saxon. This is an excerpt from the direction -- from the directive, Drina, on the use of the Army of Republika Srpska.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I have a problem. I don't have the required document on the screen, and I think I did give a correct reference.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] This is an excerpt from the directive on the use of the Army of Republika Srpska, P1555.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: You already discussed this document with Mr. Saxon. I'm going to point to page 17 in the B/C/S and page 7 in the English. General, on your copy, that would be page 8. I'm going to read the middle part and ask you to comment on that. It says in this directive of the Army of Republika Srpska, Drina: "In the event of the aggression by the Croatian Army on the Republic of Serbian Krajina or external aggression against the Republika Srpska and the other Serbian states, by a decisive defence from the border itself and on all the front lines, prevent rapid enemy penetration, the cutting off the RS territory and crushing of the Army of Republika Srpska. Immediately send and resubordinate a part of the forces (six brigades) to the Main Staff of the Serbian Army of the Krajina to be engaged as decided by the commander of the Main Staff of the Army of the Serbian Krajina. While part of the forces (two brigades) are to immediately cross the Sava river, take mounts Papuk and Pakracka Gora in coordinated action with the 8th Corps of the Serbian Army of Krajina and create conditions for further offensive operations." General, this is my question to you: We all know in this courtroom, we have heard evidence and you also testified, that in early May 1995 the Croatian Army - I'm going to use the term - attacked the area of the Serbian Republic of Krajina in an operation called "Flash." Are you aware that when the Serbian -- the Republic of the Serbian Krajina --

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Could the counsel please be asked to repeat his question.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Sorry, just a second. The interpreters would like you to please restate your question.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I apologise to the interpreters.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Are you aware that when the -- when Croatia attacked the Serbian Republic of the Krajina in the Flash operation in 1995 in May, that the Army of Republika Srpska sent any unit or resubordinated any of its units to the Serbian Army of the Krajina, as it was supposed to have done, according to what I have just read to you?

utterances.speaker: MIODRAG SIMIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Had it been like that, Mr. Lukic, the situation in Western Slavonia would have been quite different. Evidently, this did not happen.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: The short answer is [Microphone not activated]

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] That is correct, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Let's try to go for the short answers all the time.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: If there exists a directive, which we heard was one of the most important documents for command and control, and if it envisaged for a commander of a unit to take certain action and if the commander fails to act upon the directive and in the part that refers to him, then there should be some repercussions applied in relation to that commander?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Mr. Saxon.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: That is clearly a leading question, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: The objection is that it's clearly a leading question.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: Questions could be rephrased: What happens if the commander fails to act upon the directive.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I accept that.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Lukic [Microphone not activated]

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I may still be in the mode that I worked with for the past year. I apologise.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: What are the consequences of the omission to implementing the provisions of the directive under the proviso that the directive holds the force that it does?

utterances.speaker: MIODRAG SIMIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: The directive was produced in the month of December of 1994. We know when Flash took place. The military and political situation changed. It was up to the commander of the Main Staff to decide whether he was going to fully implement the directive in the relevant part or not, which depended on the developments. If the commanders refused to go there, then that would be considered a crime, a criminal offence.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Thank you. I will be moving to a different topic. I have finished with this line of questions related to the Drina Plan. Mr. Saxon put a number of questions to you and showed a number of documents to you which deal with the fact that the Army of Yugoslavia did not conduct itself in accordance with the sanctions that were imposed by the FRY in relation to Republika Srpska. You will recall the documents that were put to you on this issue.

utterances.speaker: MIODRAG SIMIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: You were also shown a document where the amount of 500.000 dinars was mentioned as having been given to the Army of the Republika Srpska. Based on this, Mr. Saxon suggested that this was an indication of the fact that the sanctions had not been implemented in the way that had been publicly presented. Do you recall?

utterances.speaker: MIODRAG SIMIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Can we look at document P2817. I have a hard copy for the General.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: General, please have a look at the document. I'm interested in the first paragraph only, but you can read the entire document. This is a document which was signed by General Ratko Mladic in November of 1994. It's a document of the Main Staff of the Army of the Republika Srpska, the sector for administration and personnel affairs. Please follow me, and I'm going to be reading paragraph 1 and asking for your comments. The heading is: Current status of professional servicemen and civilians in the VRS. "The abolishment of salaries for professional servicemen, civilians, officers, and contract soldiers of the VRS has caused difficult existential situation for their families. Members of this army consider the act to be immoral and absurd, especially because they are fighting for the honourable cause of defending the Serbian people and saving the Serbian state and not for anything else. It is difficult to foresee all of the individual suffering and reactions to this decision." On reading the document, can you conclude if the sanctions were actual or -- were real or not?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: [Previous translation continues] ... it is not. Thank you, I'm sorry.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Could I hear the question again? I was reading the text.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Based on what you've read, can you conclude that the sanctions that were imposed on Republika Srpska and the Army of Republika Srpska, were they really in place when it came to their salaries or not?

utterances.speaker: MIODRAG SIMIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. They really were in place.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] We will have to move into private session for the next topic.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: May the Chamber please move into private session.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: We're in private session, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Thank you so much. Yes, Mr. Lukic.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: You will also recall Mr. Saxon showing you a number of documents concerning material aid being sent by the Republic of Serbia to the VRS between the period of August and June. We have the 19th of June, the 1st of September, all of 1995.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Saxon.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: I'm very sorry to interrupt but the translation reads of the question: "You will also recall Mr. Saxon showing you a number of documents concerning material aid being sent by the Republic of Serbia to the VRS." I guess Mr. Lukic is seeing the problem.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] The Army of Yugoslavia was what I said. I think I said that, but I apologise to the interpreters if they were unable to follow me.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
