utterances.text: General, I will now show you a document. This is P749, minutes from the 36th Session of the VSO. I think that the document is under seal.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: [Previous translation continues] ...

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] We are in private session, are we not? [In English] P749. [Interpretation] I will have to be reading from my copy.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Sit down, General. I will be reading for your benefit. Do not worry. This is minutes from the 36th Session of the VSO, held on the 12th of May, 1995. If we turn to the next page, page 2 of the B/C/S, which is, I think, the same page in English, and could we look at the bottom part of the page. This is Mr. Perisic speaking now where he says, among other things: "We believe that the Croatian Army, the GS, which I believe is the Main Staff, will attack along the axis leading to Bihac in order to cut off the RSK territory and execute the -- or implement the Z-4 plan while P/S which is probably --"

utterances.speaker: MIODRAG SIMIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Auxiliary forces.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Right, so what we had before were main forces probably. "Would go along the Baranja axis. An attack by the HV can be expected by the middle of this month, depending mostly on the position of Croatia's sponsors." So I was quoting Mr. Perisic.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Could we have the last page of the document where the VSO conclusions are listed. Could we have the previous page in the English version, my apologies.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: I'm reading conclusion number 9: "Lend certain assistance to the armies of the RSK and RS within limits that do not compromise the combat readiness of the Army of Yugoslavia." General, this is a conclusion by the Supreme Defence Council taken at its session held on the 12th of May, 1995. Can you explain why it was that the VSO took this decision, and what was the obligation on the part of Mr. Perisic in relation to the VSO decision?

utterances.speaker: MIODRAG SIMIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: The VSO's assessment was that the army needed to be assisted, and the chief of the General Staff did not have the power, as I've already said, to use the resources and assets without the decision of the commander in-chief - in this case, that's the VSO. That's why the particular problem was raised by him, in order for him to get a certain response.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: We're talking about the 12th of May, 1995. Was the attack on RSK in the form of Flash a threat to the security of the Army of Yugoslavia?

utterances.speaker: MIODRAG SIMIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: By that time, on the 12th of May, Flash had already been finished. What was to follow next was Baranja, the 11th -- the 11th Corps which borders directly with the Federal Republic of Yugoslavia. In that context assistance needed to be provided in order to avert any security risks for the FRY in order to prevent fire from spreading, so to speak, to the territory of the Federal Republic of Yugoslavia.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Can we now call up document - and let us stay in private session, Your Honour - P736 [sic]. These are minutes from the 39th Session of the Supreme Defence Council held on the 29th of July, 1995. 763. [In English] P763.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] General, the document is similar to the previous one.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Could we turn to page 2 of the English version, the beginning of the page, and the B/C/S version, we will -- we will have to turn to the following page.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: So, General, we have the minutes from the meeting of the Supreme Defence Council held on 29th of July, 1995, which, under item 1 reads -- no, I'm sorry, I made a mistake.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Can we turn to the previous page, please. We need the bottom part of the document, and the same goes for the English version. It reads: "Item 1, the conclusions from the assessment of the current military and political situation in the region and proposed measures for strengthening the security and defence of the Federal Republic of Yugoslavia were presented by the chief of the General Staff of the Army of Yugoslavia, Colonel General Momcilo Perisic. According to the assessment of General Perisic with the development of the situation in the broader international arena and on the front line, the crisis in the territory of the former Yugoslavia had entered a critical stage characterised by an increasingly prominent orientation towards the war option." And then we have General Perisic speaking. Could we turn to the following page in the B/C/S. And without reading the document, I will say that three variants are referred to therein. I need the same portion of the document in English.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: I will read for you what General Perisic went on to say.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I think it's the next page in English. Mm-hm. Your Honours, I will be reading the third paragraph in English. All of this is Mr. Perisic speaking. "All the three options described are unfavorable for RS and RSK. Unless urgent and appropriate measures are taken on the political, diplomatic, and military levels, attempts might even be made to draw the FRY into the war." And, finally, could we have the last page in both English and the B/C/S where the Supreme Defence Council's conclusions are listed.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: General, do you know when did Operation Storm take place?

utterances.speaker: MIODRAG SIMIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: In the month of August of the same year, just as Flash, on the 29th.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: This VSO session was held on 29th of July, 1995, and I will be reading conclusion number 4. "The Army of Republika Srpska and the Republic of Serbian Krajina should continue to be provided certain assistance within the limits that do not impair the combat readiness of the Army of Yugoslavia." Is such a VSO conclusion binding upon General Perisic?

utterances.speaker: MIODRAG SIMIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. It is tantamount to an order issued to Mr. Perisic.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: I have completed my examination of Mr. Simic. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Mr. Lukic.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Questioned by the Court:

utterances.speaker: JUDGE DAVID
utterances.text: General --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: May the Chamber please move into open session.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: We're back in open session, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE DAVID
utterances.text: General, on Friday, the 26th of February, at page 28, lines 22, 25; page 29, lines 1 to 10, you said: "Mr. Prosecutor, once the JNA starting pulling out of BH, both armies were established. Some officers pull out members of the VJ, and then those born in Republika Srpska were sent to that army through the 30th and 40th Personnel Centres. Those centres are organisational units of the personnel administration of the General Staff. Their purpose was to have a register at one place of all those persons to enable them to claim their status-related rights." Do you remember that quotation of yours? You remember what you said?

utterances.speaker: MIODRAG SIMIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Your Honours, yes. Absolutely.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE DAVID
utterances.text: [Previous translation continues] ... in addition to this purpose to have a register, were there any other purposes, objectives, or functions that this Personnel Centres perform, according to your experience and knowledge at the time?

utterances.speaker: MIODRAG SIMIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Your Honour, I did not manage those centres directly. As far as I know, their main function was the one that I described and that you referred to just now.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE DAVID
utterances.text: In your functions in the intelligence hierarchy of the army, were you aware of any order, resolution, decree, establishing those centres, the 30th and 40th Personnel Centres? Were you ever informed of any order, resolution, decree, establishing those centres?

utterances.speaker: MIODRAG SIMIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Your Honour, from talking with senior officers, I heard that there was a decision by President Lilic and that, on the basis of that decision the chief of the General Staff was obliged to form these centres. I did not see that personally in any documents. This is not something that falls under my jurisdiction.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE DAVID
utterances.text: Thank you. Second question: You said, in relation to the close relationship among the three armies, VJ, Serbian Krajina, and Republika Srpska, that it was in the interest of the Army of Yugoslavia, page 83, lines 4 to 9 of yesterday, in order to prevent any possible surprises or threat to security. My question is: Had the centres, Personnel Centres, play any role in fostering the close relationship among the three armies, according to your experience and/or knowledge?

utterances.speaker: MIODRAG SIMIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: The transformation from the JNA, and these relationships were forged from the JNA, so these Personnel Centres did not play a significant role in forging close relationship between these three armies.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE DAVID
utterances.text: Additional question: Did these centres aim also at improving the combat readiness of the three armies in the field, according to your experience and knowledge at the time?

utterances.speaker: MIODRAG SIMIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Your Honour, it is very difficult for me to reply. If there is a record of people who voluntarily apply to go there in order to implement their entitlements, the very departure of those people there would naturally improve the combat readiness of the units which they joined.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE DAVID
utterances.text: Were you aware - additional question - of any order, resolution, decision, of the General Staff of the VJ supporting, encouraging these transfers on a selective manner encouraging these transfers on a selected manner? Yes or no?

utterances.speaker: MIODRAG SIMIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE DAVID
utterances.text: Could you give me an explanation of these measures, if you are knowledgeable of them? Elaboration, further elaboration. Please comment if you can.

utterances.speaker: MIODRAG SIMIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Your Honour, there were talks with all the people who were from that area or had some kind of connection to that area through relations or something else, how it was necessary, and in the interest of the people for them to go there, but nobody was threatened that if they refused to go or if they did not accept this position by the General Staff or the chief that they would be subject to any kind of sanction. I personally in my administration have a general who was the chief of a section and who is from Republika Srpska. He did not agree to go there, and this was not something that proved to be an obstacle for him to attain the rank of a general in the Army. So I don't know whether this is something that the public should know about or not.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE DAVID
utterances.text: [Previous translation continues] ... some officers that did not perform well in the field during the combat of the war were returned to the VJ through the 30th or 40th Personnel Centres, were you aware, because of failure on objectives of the war, in accomplishing objective of the war?

utterances.speaker: MIODRAG SIMIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Your Honour, I am not aware of these matters. I was not really informed about that. As an operative, I had major tasks to perform that I was busy with during the day and during the night, so I'm not really able to give you an answer about that.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE DAVID
utterances.text: [Previous translation continues] ...

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Any questions arising from the questions by the Bench, Mr. Lukic?

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Just one clarification. Judge David, on page 53, line 19 said: "In your functions in the intelligence hierarchy," and the witness did give an answer. Further cross-examination by Mr. Lukic:

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Mr. Simic, were you in the operative or the intelligence hierarchy?

utterances.speaker: MIODRAG SIMIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I did notice that word. But I thought that His Honour meant my operative function, not intelligence function. This is why I did not intervene.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Mr. Saxon.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: Nothing, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Thank you so much. Mr. Simic, we've come to the conclusion of your testimony. I'm sure you're looking forward to going back home. Thank you so much for coming to testify at the Tribunal, and you really stayed here for quite a long time, much longer than expected. And on behalf of the Tribunal, thank you so much, and travel well back home. You are now excused. You may stand down.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Your Honour, for your professional attitude.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Mr. Lukic.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] The Defence is ready to call its next witness, Mr. Nikolic. I don't know if the time is sufficient to take this witness out and to bring the next witness in. Perhaps there isn't enough time for that. Perhaps it would be better to go on a break. I'm in your hands, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Thank you. We will take you in our hands and send you on a break and come back at a quarter to 6.00. Court adjourned.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Mr. Lukic, before you call the next witness, could we deal with a little point on housekeeping? The cases of Seselj and Karadzic are not sitting tomorrow. We were originally not going to be sitting because there was no court available. Would the parties be in a position to sit tomorrow? It looks like it will have to -- if we do, it will be in the morning.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I have been leading the witness we have just finished with, and I will be leading the next witness. In view of the situation, I was planning to work on the proofing of the witness tomorrow morning. If you so decide, I will comply with your ruling and lead the witness tomorrow. Unfortunately, this is the way Mr. Guy-Smith and I divided work so that I will be dealing with this next witness as well.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: [Previous translation continues] ... proofing before he coming into testify?

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: By that he means not only the witness we're about to see today but also the witness we will be seeing after the witness who is to testify. He has decided to take on a relatively heavy burden.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: He's a strong man, you can see. Okay.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: Indeed so.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: It does seem as if, therefore, that it's not convenient for you to sit tomorrow morning. Okay. If that is the case, so be it. We will then not sit. You may call the witness.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you very much, Your Honours. I call Mr. Stamenko Nikolic as our next Defence witness.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: May the witness please make the declaration.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I solemnly declare that I will speak the truth, the whole truth, and nothing but the truth.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Thank you so much, Mr. Nikolic. You may be seated. And good afternoon to you.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you. Good afternoon, Your Honours. I am honoured to extend my greetings to you and all the staff present in the courtroom.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Thank you so much. Mr. Lukic.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Will you please state your full name for the record.

utterances.speaker: STAMENKO NIKOLIC
utterances.text: Stamenko Nikolic.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: General, I will now be going through your career by presenting the information I have, and I expect you to confirm that they are true or not, in order to go through this as quickly as possible. Right at the start, let me draw your attention to the following, General. Please make a brief pause before answering my question. I've told you as much during proofing, but we need to be mindful of the speed for the sake of the interpreters.

utterances.speaker: STAMENKO NIKOLIC
utterances.text: That's quite clear.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: You were born in 1948 near Vranje; is that right?

utterances.speaker: STAMENKO NIKOLIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: You are now lieutenant-general in retirement?

utterances.speaker: STAMENKO NIKOLIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: You graduated from the Military Academy in 1970 in the Department of Ground Forces, specifically artillery rocket units; is that right?

utterances.speaker: STAMENKO NIKOLIC
utterances.text: Yes. I want to only point out that these were anti-aircraft defence artillery rocket units.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: You graduated the Command and Staff School in -- from the Command Staff School in 1983; is that right?

utterances.speaker: STAMENKO NIKOLIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: And you graduated from the Operations Command Staff School in 1990. That's the highest educational institution, is it not?

utterances.speaker: STAMENKO NIKOLIC
utterances.text: The highest level school in the army in Yugoslavia was the Operations School, as you indicated, which is, in fact, the School of People's Defence.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: You graduated from the Faculty of Law in 1987; is that right?

utterances.speaker: STAMENKO NIKOLIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Let me go through the various positions you held in your career. Up until 1984, you were serving in several garrisons; is that right?

utterances.speaker: STAMENKO NIKOLIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: In 1984, you joined the Federal Secretariat for National Defence where you were desk officer, specialist for housing policy in the 3rd Division of the then-personnel administration of the SSNO; is that right?

utterances.speaker: STAMENKO NIKOLIC
utterances.text: Yes. I did not merely join; I was transferred to that position.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Thank you. My apologies for lack of precision. You were appointed to the position of the chief of that particular department, or division, in 1991, whereupon you were appointed chief of a department which, in 1992, as part of reorganisation, became administration for system-related and status-related affairs with the Ministry of Defence of the Federal Republic of Yugoslavia; is that right?

utterances.speaker: STAMENKO NIKOLIC
utterances.text: Yes. Yes, it was a sector for system and status-related affairs and legal affairs as well.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: We will be going through the specific institutions later on, and we'll have an opportunity to explain them. In July 1994, you became chief of the administration for system and status-related affairs with the Ministry of Defence; is that right?

utterances.speaker: STAMENKO NIKOLIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: You held that position up until the end of December 1995 when you were transferred to the General Staff of the Army of Yugoslavia, the position of the chief of the independent administration for housing affairs, unless I'm mistaken, which was an autonomous administration with the VJ General Staff at the time; is that right?

utterances.speaker: STAMENKO NIKOLIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Then you became the chief of the personnel administration of the sector for cadres, mobilisation and system matters of the Army -- of the General Staff of the Army of Yugoslavia. You took up this post in March 2000 -- no, I made a mistake. This was in 1998.

utterances.speaker: STAMENKO NIKOLIC
utterances.text: I became chief of the personnel administration on the 31st of December, 1998. And I became the chief of the sector or deputy -- assistant chief of the General Staff for mobilisation, staffing and system matters on the 8th of March, 2000.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: And you remained at that post until July 2000, when you submitted your request for retirement; is that right?

utterances.speaker: STAMENKO NIKOLIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: We're going to cover that when we go through the specific topics. But you had the rank of colonel in December 1991; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: STAMENKO NIKOLIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: You became major-general in December 1996, on the 31st of December, 1996?

utterances.speaker: STAMENKO NIKOLIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: And, finally, you became lieutenant-general in December 1999; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: STAMENKO NIKOLIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Mr. Nikolic, I'm going to begin from the moment you moved to the SSNO. This was in 1984. And then that became the Ministry of Defence once the Army of Yugoslavia was formed. Can you tell us briefly what your sector's duties were in the Federal Secretariat for National Defence, the SSNO, in that period before it became the JNA.

utterances.speaker: STAMENKO NIKOLIC
utterances.text: My first post in the SSNO was to be the chief of the department for housing policy in the Yugoslav People's Army. As you said yourself, after that, I became the chief of the third department, which was called the department for the standard and status of military and civilian personnel serving in the Yugoslav People's Army. The main duties of the sector for housing policy was to analyse, assess the status, record and register requests, monitor the number of unresolved housing cases, and to propose legal solutions, in order to be able to provide housing for all members of the JNA. Later this was called the rules on the resolution of housing problems of professional members of the military. After being appointed to the head of the third section, which was part of the then-personnel administration of the Federal Secretariat for National Defence as an independent administration, our tasks were systemic solutions or, to put it differently, normative regulation of the system from the area of the status, situation in the service, and the standards of professional members of the military. However, after the transformation occurred and it became the Army of Yugoslavia, after the section became an administration, pursuant to the rules on the authority and the jurisdiction of organisational units of the SSNO, its duties were broadened and had to do with a number of tasks stemming from the Federal Secretariat for National Defence and the federal government, and this was regulating the situation in the service, the status in the service, the housing policy in a somewhat different form. Also, it dealt with education and, as part of that, scientific activities, as well as salaries and other elements of the service, without having to go into each one.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: General, just one correction. This last thing that you mentioned, and I'm making the correction on line 63 -- on page 63, lines 1 and 2 when you said: When this transformed into the administration, and this was after the federal Ministry of Defence of the Federal Republic of Yugoslavia was formed, just one moment, please, from that point on when the Army of Yugoslavia was formed, when the new constitution was adopted, did the Federal Secretariat for National Defence continue to exist? Just answer briefly, please.

utterances.speaker: STAMENKO NIKOLIC
utterances.text: After the decision was adopted to transform the Army of Yugoslavia, there was a complete separation of the Ministry of Defence and the Army of Yugoslavia. At that point in time, two organisational units were created with special authority, jurisdiction, and duties.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Very well. We will discuss that separately. In any case, is it true that the Federal Secretariat for National Defence did not exist anymore, the forming -- with the forming of a new state and the adoption of a new constitution in 1992 and with the forming of the Ministry of Defence?

utterances.speaker: STAMENKO NIKOLIC
utterances.text: Yes, that is correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Thank you. In the previous period, while the Federal Secretariat for National Defence still existed, where was the General Staff located? Can you please just be as brief as possible.

utterances.speaker: STAMENKO NIKOLIC
utterances.text: In the earlier period, as you indicated yourself, the General Staff of the Army of Yugoslavia practically represented a sector of the Federal Secretariat for National Defence, and the federal Ministry for National Defence was practically superior to the General Staff of the Army of Yugoslavia.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: As compared to the General Staff of the Yugoslav People's Army.

utterances.speaker: STAMENKO NIKOLIC
utterances.text: Yes, that is correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Can we now look at document 65 ter of the Defence, 01115D; three 1s, 5D.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: General, I prepared for you a binder in the order of the documents that I considered to be correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I would like to have this binder shown to the Prosecution. And can we go to page 2 of this document right away. Your Honours, this is a diagram.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: General, please look at page 2, that's right. Since we will be looking at another document, talking about the jurisdiction of specific organisational units, I would just like for us here in the courtroom, particularly for the Trial Chamber, to see how -- or to get an impression of how the Ministry of Defence functioned by looking at this diagram. General, we first see in the middle the Ministry of Defence - this is the federal Ministry of Defence. I assume that this is it not dispute. What is the relationship here of the Ministry of Defence with the General Staff of the Yugoslav Army?

utterances.speaker: STAMENKO NIKOLIC
utterances.text: Based on this diagram, as you indicated - this is page 2 of the document - it can be concluded without any doubt that the minister of defence was no longer superior to the General Staff of the Army of Yugoslavia. These dotted lines that you see indicate that there is coordination between them, but not in terms of the chain of command. These are separate bodies.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: We also see that the minister of defence has subordinated to him several organisational units. They are immediately subordinated to the Ministry of Defence as sectors. Some are in the form of administrations, independent administrations. I'm interested, in a couple of words only, where the organisational unit where you worked was located.

utterances.speaker: STAMENKO NIKOLIC
utterances.text: My organisational unit was the sector for the systemic status and legal affairs, and it's shown here that it was immediately subordinated to the minister of defence. This sector comprised of three administrations: The sector administration; the system and status issues administration where I was the head; and the legal administration, which was headed by Starcevic. Starcevic Miodrag. That's right; I had forgotten the name.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: There is an administration for finance and budget. This was also an independent administration that was directly subordinated to the minister of defence with all of its departments and sections?

utterances.speaker: STAMENKO NIKOLIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Very well. I apologise to the Prosecution if this was leading the witness, but I would like to cover this diagram as soon as possible so that we don't get into complicated questions.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] All right. I would like to tender this document, Your Honour, please.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: The document is admitted into evidence. May it please be given an exhibit number.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honours. This document shall be assigned Exhibit Number D239. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: General, this diagram that we have just looked at, is that how the Ministry of Defence functioned for as long as you were there, since the time the ministry was formed and subsequently?

utterances.speaker: STAMENKO NIKOLIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Well, we could be even more specific, although I believe that this is clear to the Court. When was the federal Ministry of Defence formed, and since when did it function in this particular way that is demonstrated on the diagram?

utterances.speaker: STAMENKO NIKOLIC
utterances.text: The Ministry of Defence was formed in June 1992, in the form that it is shown on this diagram.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Can we now please look at another document. Can we put it up on the screen, and we would like to point out to the Trial Chamber some important organisational units. With the help of this document, this is document 65 ter 01113D. This is from the 65 ter list of documents. These are the rules on the jurisdiction of the organisational units of the Ministry of Defence.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Have you found it?

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I have a suggestion by my client here. The secretariat -- actually the Registry has said that the previous number was an MFI number. This is what it says in the transcript on page 66, line 11. I hope that we are looking at the correct document and that it is not an MFI document.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: On page 11, I don't see the word MFI -- oh, marked for identification. Yeah, it ought to come off. It is not marked for identification, it is admitted. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, yes, that is what I saw as well.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: [Previous translation continues] ...

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Mr. Nikolic, what do we see now in front of us?

utterances.speaker: STAMENKO NIKOLIC
utterances.text: All right. With the order or the rules on the responsibilities of the organisational units in the federal defence ministry, the responsibilities are set of certain sectors and independent administrations as organisational units of the Ministry of Defence.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Can we look at Article 4, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: This is the rules on the responsibilities of the organisational units. I would like to have your comment on Article 4 of these rules.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] In the B/C/S this is page 5 and in the English, also page 5.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Before that, General, perhaps we could just give us a brief comment on the preamble and the grounds for adopting these rules.

utterances.speaker: STAMENKO NIKOLIC
utterances.text: These rules were adopted pursuant to Article 109, para 3, of the Law on All People's Defence, and pursuant to the order of -- on the delegation of certain powers held or vested with the Federal Secretariat for National Defence onto the Yugoslav People's Army.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Thank you. I'm asking you about these rules which were adopted at the time when a new constitution was already in place. However, the rules and regulations from the previous system were still being applied. Why was this the case?

utterances.speaker: STAMENKO NIKOLIC
utterances.text: At the time the rules were adopted governing the responsibilities of the organisational units of the Ministry of Defence. The Law on the Army of Yugoslavia had not yet been adopted. It was still in parliamentary procedure, and the process was ongoing. The process -- the legislative process takes a certain period of time. In order for a vacuum to be avoided, the Presidency of the FRY took a decision on the 19th of May, 1992 to rename the Yugoslav People's Army into the -- to rename the Yugoslav People's Army the Army of Yugoslavia. Do you need any additional explanation?

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Yes, please.

utterances.speaker: STAMENKO NIKOLIC
utterances.text: Paragraph 2 of the order, as far as I remember, reads explicitly: "Until such time as the Law on the Army of Yugoslavia is adopted, because this was laid down in the 27th of April, 1992 constitution, the legislation that was in force up until that date would be applicable."

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: We will be looking at another piece of legislation later on. Do you know, approximately, when the Law on Defence of the Federal Republic of Yugoslavia was adopted?

utterances.speaker: STAMENKO NIKOLIC
utterances.text: If you will allow me, I should like to put these papers together. I'm not that skillful with the papers. I seem to have mixed them up. Since the FRY constitution of the 27th of April, 1992, which came into force forthwith, as soon as it was carried, defined in precise terms --

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Can you please move on to my question. Do you know when the Law on Defence was adopted?

utterances.speaker: STAMENKO NIKOLIC
utterances.text: On the same date when the Law on the Army was adopted. And this was on the 6th of November, 1993.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: We will get back to what you wanted to discuss later. I should like to have your comments on Article 4 of the order. What is the basis on which organisational units of the Ministry of Defence would act?

utterances.speaker: STAMENKO NIKOLIC
utterances.text: I apologise. The -- Article 4 does not relate to the order, but, rather, to the rules of -- governing these responsibilities. Article 4 defines in clear terms that organisational units shall engage in activities within their remit based on federal laws and other laws governing the work of the Ministry of Defence, based on acts issued by the President of the Republic of the FRY, based on documents issued by the Supreme Defence Council and the enactments of the minister of defence, who shall direct his staff to act in accordance with the legislation in force.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Who is the Ministry of Defence subordinated to, in a word, please?

utterances.speaker: STAMENKO NIKOLIC
utterances.text: The Ministry of Defence as a federal organ is subordinated to the federal government.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Let us move on to Article 12 which is page 6 in the B/C/S and page 7 in the English. We will be discussing specific organisational unit. First off, the sector for system and status-related issues and legal affairs, which was the sector your administration was part of. Article 12 provides for the competences of the various sectors. And can you tell us what were the competences of the sector you were part of?

utterances.speaker: STAMENKO NIKOLIC
utterances.text: The sector for system and status-related issues and legal affairs - I apologise, I was waiting for the interpretation - performs business of administrative and specialist nature which have to do -- which has to do with the analysis of system-related solutions, which were provided for by laws or bylaws and relate to finding systemic solutions for the status of professional servicemen, the state of affairs in the army, social security with the emphasis on health insurance, as well as pension and disability insurance. Systemic solutions are -- were supposed to be found for housing of the servicemen of the Army of Yugoslavia.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Let's move on to your administration which is covered by Article 13. I'm interested in one of the duties listed in item 2 where it is stated that the administration for system and status-related issues, that the administration will do what? Can you tell us?

utterances.speaker: STAMENKO NIKOLIC
utterances.text: The rules on responsibilities --

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Pause there a moment. It's Article 13.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Can we have the next page? That's what I want the witness to explain. Item 2. The same goes for the English version. Can we have the next page for Their Honours to follow. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: General, can we have your comments on what it was that you did in your administration in connection with this particular item of the rules -- of the rules.

utterances.speaker: STAMENKO NIKOLIC
utterances.text: The administration that I headed in 1994 was the basic tactical body responsible for regulations governing salaries, pecuniary allowances, and other sorts of remuneration in the army in accordance with the Law on the Army of Yugoslavia.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Once you've done the preparatory work for one such bylaw, who would be the person signing it?

utterances.speaker: STAMENKO NIKOLIC
utterances.text: The powers in relation to the adoption of bylaws were defined by the law. It is, in fact, the Law on the Army of Yugoslavia. Article 87 of the law regulates in no uncertain terms that the federal government shall, by way of its regulations specify the amount of salaries to be paid out, the salary scales, the titles of various allowances, and all other manner of remuneration paid in the army. In addition to laws governing salaries, where Articles 81 -- or, rather, 71 to 79 of the law, basic principles governing salaries were laid out. So in addition the law, the federal government issues a decree on the salaries of professional servicemen where it regulates in detail the way in which other entitlements are defined and the way in which they are paid, as well as all the other matters that need to be regulated in order for salaries to be paid out. Now, the minister of defence, as a part of the federal body, is also entitled under the army -- under the Law of the Army of Bosnia-Herzegovina to issue a more detailed rules governing allowances, reimbursements of expenses, and other income in the army, and this particular body of law or bylaw, is called rules.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Thank you, General. Can we have your brief comment on Article 14, which deals with legal administration? Item 4 says that: "The legal affairs administration shall provide opinions and legal matters in the application of laws and other regulations?" What does it mean? Who does the administration provide these opinions to; and are these opinions binding in any way?

utterances.speaker: STAMENKO NIKOLIC
utterances.text: As I said at the beginning, the legal affairs administration is part of the sector for system and status-related issues. As the body best placed to deal with these matters, because it is a legal service, gives its opinion on all the enactments issued by the Ministry of Defence or, rather, organisational units of the Ministry of Defence as to their compatibility with the constitution and all the relevant legislation in the country. Let me point out one thing. The legal affairs administration is not competent in terms of amending the legal texts that come from the Ministry of Defence or the General Staff of the Army of Yugoslavia, the legal text governing material entitlements. And if you want me to, if Their Honours want me to do, I can explain what these material entitlements are.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Just pause there for a moment. Tell us what these material entitlements are.

utterances.speaker: STAMENKO NIKOLIC
utterances.text: Right. These material solutions are proposals given by the organisational units of the VJ General Staff and the Ministry of Defence, bodies which are the tactically responsible bodies for the workings of the army and the workings of the ministry. Let me give you an example. If the commander of the air force, an anti-aircraft defence wants an allowance to be introduced for pilots, let's, say, to be paid out as part of their salary, and if he proposes a solution whereby the amount to be paid out - this is merely an example I'm giving you - should be at the level of a junior lieutenant's salary, by rank and by position, in that case, this sort of proposal would be forwarded to the administration for system and status-related issues. The regulations are formulated and specific solutions proposed; whereas, the chief of the legal affairs administration shall, on the basis of the powers vested with him, this piece of regulation is in keeping with the law or is contrary to the law. In short, that is his role.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Next we have the sector for economic, military economic activity. I will not be dealing with this issue. But do you happen to know who headed the sector for military economic affairs?

utterances.speaker: STAMENKO NIKOLIC
utterances.text: Well, it's been 19 years since then but I do know who it was. This was Kadijevic, but not Veljko Kadijevic, but a man with the same last name, a lieutenant-general.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Radojca?

utterances.speaker: STAMENKO NIKOLIC
utterances.text: Yes, Radojca.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: I would like to comment on a different organisational unit, which I think has something to do with your unit, this is the administration for finances and budget. This is Article 23.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, on the e-court copy, this is page -- page 14 in the English.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, I've found it.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Again, General, I don't want to talk about a document which is quite clear by itself. But I would like you to tell us, in your own words, something about this Article 4, item 4, as far as the tasks of the administration for finance and budget is concerned.

utterances.speaker: STAMENKO NIKOLIC
utterances.text: I cannot read it.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: I will read it. I will read it slowly. Just listen. So the finance and budget administration in item 4 it states: "It shall monitor the implementation of the military budget and in this regard, propose all necessary measures to ensure financial discipline and the regular flow of funds from the federal budget." Just in a couple of words, General. What is the military budget, and what is the federal budget, and what is the role of this administration?

utterances.speaker: STAMENKO NIKOLIC
utterances.text: The finance and budget administration is an independent administration, an independent organisational unit, rather, of the Ministry of Defence, and it bears the greatest responsibility as far as the preparation and the drafting of the budget is concerned. Budget for the Army of Yugoslavia and for the Ministry of Defence. Would you permit me to clarify further?

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: STAMENKO NIKOLIC
utterances.text: In the Law on Financing of the Federal Republic of Yugoslavia, the term "a single budget" is used. There aren't two budgets. It is still -- there isn't a separate military budget, but the person who will draft the military budget and deal with the taking of the necessary measures and implementing -- or -- financial discipline, and financial discipline means the expenditure of only the amount of funds granted by the Assembly or the Law on the Federal Budget.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Microphone, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: In item 10 of the same article - perhaps we can turn to the next page, please; this is item 10 - this finance and budget administration is said to be in charge of the defence ministry's accounting centre and exercises professional control over its work. General, can you please explain what the accounting centre of the defence ministry was, how did it function in the JNA and after the forming of the Army of Yugoslavia?

utterances.speaker: STAMENKO NIKOLIC
utterances.text: In order to be able to answer this question, I'm sorry, I just need to remind you of item 7 because 10 is related to item 7. It's not necessary to read it.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Yes, are you correct.

utterances.speaker: STAMENKO NIKOLIC
utterances.text: You don't read the whole item, but it says: Financing the beneficiaries of the budget, the calculation or processing, and the paying out of salaries. That means that the finance and -- and budget administration is only responsible for the calculation and payment of salaries to all members of the army, and that is why this accounting centre was formed in the federal Ministry of Defence, which is directly connected to the finance and budget administration, without going into too much detail, because that would require a lot of time. This is the centre which collects all the data on all the professional members of the army, calculates the salaries according to the specific regulations, and also issues those salaries.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: During the SFRY and the old JNA, if I can put it that way, was there an accounting centre of the General Staff of the Army of Yugoslavia and after the Army of Yugoslavia was formed, were there any other functions that it had in relation to issuing the salaries of members of the Army of Yugoslavia?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: [Previous translation continues] ...

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] We have a clarification here for the Trial Chamber, and the interpreters perhaps can help. We have two terms in the Serbian which in the English language are translated as the same. I would like to stress that there is a term called racunski centar of the General Staff, and the accounting racunovodstveni centar of the Army of Yugoslavia General Staff. I actually said the Ministry of Defence at the end.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: So, General, there is a distinction here. Perhaps it would be best if you explained what the body was before the Army of Yugoslavia was formed and who issued salaries before that, and what happened once the Army of Yugoslavia and the Ministry of Defence were formed.

utterances.speaker: STAMENKO NIKOLIC
utterances.text: When the Yugoslav People's Army still existed and while the Law on Service in the Armed Forces was still in force and when the General Staff of the Army of the Armed Forces was subordinated to the federal minister of defence, there was an accounting centre in that General Staff racunovodstveni centar. However, with the forming of the Ministry of Defence, as a separate federal organ of the federal government the racunovodstveni centar was formed in the budget and finance administration, and then it took over all the responsibilities of the previous racunovodstveni centar. If Your Honours would allow me to explain the terms used, the difference between racunovodstveni centar and a racunski centar.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Just one moment we have a problem with what it says on page 77, line 8.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: [Previous translation continues] ...

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I think that the English translation is not good.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: [Previous translation continues] ... I guess we having a problem that Madam interpreter is giving this accounting centre names still in the B/C/S, and it is very difficult without spelling the word to -- to the stenographer to stay what is being said.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: The interpreters note that we did not use the word JNA barracks. The word barracks was not said.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: [Previous translation continues] ... I understand that. You've used the word racunovska [phoen] or something like that and something similar to that.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: We also note that the witness used the same word while giving the distinction. In both times he used racunovodstveni centar.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Indeed. We are waiting for the English translation of that word.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: It is the accounting centre. Racunovodstveni centar means accounting centre. Racunski centar can mean IT centre as in computer centre, and it can also mean accounting centre, so the second word racunski can mean either one of those things.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Thank you very much, madam interpreter.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you to the interpreters. I did hear that, and I agree with the explanation. Actually the gist is actually how salaries were issued during the JNA and how salaries were issued when the Army of Yugoslavia was formed.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: So, General, I would kindly ask you to explain that in the simplest language based on what you know. So could you please give us a comparison of how the salaries were issued in first one and then the other of these time-periods?

utterances.speaker: STAMENKO NIKOLIC
utterances.text: I explained what the racunovodstveni centars do, one and the other. During the validity of the Law on the Armed Forces their role was the same. I just referred to the term of the racunski centar. This is practically a branch of the accounting, racunovodstveni centar, most simply put.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: After the Army of Yugoslavia was formed, was there an accounting centre in the General Staff and what was its function if it did have any function in terms of the salaries or responsibilities in that sense towards the Army of Yugoslavia?

utterances.speaker: STAMENKO NIKOLIC
utterances.text: The General Staff of the Army of Yugoslavia did not have an accounting centre that would process and pay out salaries. This responsibility was carried out by the accounting centre of the Ministry of Defence.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Was there -- did the General Staff have an accounting centre, and if it did, what were its responsibilities and duties?

utterances.speaker: STAMENKO NIKOLIC
utterances.text: I am going to try to explain this by giving examples. Earlier I talked about the adoption of the budget and who was responsible for drafting the budget for the Army of Yugoslavia. When the defence minister issues a decision on the amount of financial means that would be allocated from the budget to the Army of Yugoslavia, that is what we referred to as pie. All of those funds are managed by the 5th Administration of the General Staff of the Army of Yugoslavia which does not have the accounting centre, but it has the computer centre or calculating centre. So for all purposes, that is like a treasury or a safe where data is collected as to how much money goes where.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: And which funds are used for the payment of salaries, or how are salaries issued? Through which channels?

utterances.speaker: STAMENKO NIKOLIC
utterances.text: The accounting centre of the defence ministry issues salaries through chequing accounts or Giro accounts, if that's what you were asking me.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: [Previous translation continues] ... question. When this computer centre --

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Go ahead, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Thank you. When this computer centre has calculated what amount must go to the salaries of the Army of the -- of Yugoslavia, what does it do with those calculations? In other words, does it send them to the accounting centre of the Ministry of Defence who then pays, or what happens?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, perhaps I wasn't clear enough. The calculation centre of the 5th Administration, that is part of the General Staff, does not distribute any money. This is done by the accounting centre of the Ministry of Defence.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: I understand that -- [Microphone not activated]

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Which keeps and maintains financial data cards. That's how we refer to them. And these cards are kept only in this centre.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: [Previous translation continues]... okay. Let me ask my question slightly differently. What is the purpose of the calculations that are made in the computer centre of the 5th Administration? What is done with those documents -- with those calculations, or what's happened to them?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I said a little bit earlier that this calculation centre keeps records about the funds made available to it for its use. Detailed questions, the method of work, Your Honour, that they used, the criteria, this is something that is not really in my remit, so I would not be able to give you a valid explanation.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Let's look at the inspections by the Ministry of Defence. This is Article 24. I'm interested in the analysis of Article 26.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Can we please turn to the next page.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: And can you please tell us, General, what the material, financial and market inspections are, and what that involves? Have you found it?

utterances.speaker: STAMENKO NIKOLIC
utterances.text: Yes. Just let me look through these papers.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: It's Article 26. What is the material, financial, and market inspection?

utterances.speaker: STAMENKO NIKOLIC
utterances.text: Material, financial, and market inspection is a professional organ that carries out inspections primarily those involving the storage, use, and disposition of the assets of the Yugoslav Army and control the financial operations including the earlier-referred-to methods, including the consequences referred to, checking the contracts involving procurement of food, other materiel, with the exception of salaries, because that is not under the jurisdiction of the General Staff. So that organ would behave pursuant to all the regulations.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: You said not including the salaries, because that is what they are authorised for. Does the financial and market inspection also control the manner of the distribution of the salaries; and, if it does, where does it carry out these inspections?

utterances.speaker: STAMENKO NIKOLIC
utterances.text: I said that it controls financial operations in the Army of Yugoslavia. This is why I said "without including the salaries." However, this same material, financial, and market inspection is also obliged to inspect the final calculation of the salaries, but in the administration for budget and finances at the accounting centre of the Ministry of Defence. I apologise, because is this the inspection of the defence minister? That is immediately subordinated to the minister of defence.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: We will discuss this matter a little bit more. We have to stop. I do have a few more questions relating to this inspection, but this is something that we can discuss tomorrow -- actually, the day after tomorrow.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I am not going to tender this document now because I would like to comment a little more on it with the witness.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Thank you very much, Mr. Lukic. Mr. Nikolic, we are not done with you. You will have to come -- unfortunately, we are not able to sit tomorrow because there is no court available, but we will sitting on Thursday in the morning at 9.00 in Courtroom I, which is this courtroom. If you can be back here on Thursday at 9.00 in the morning. In the meantime, while you are out of the witness-stand, you are not allowed, now that you have started testifying, to discuss this case with anybody; in particular, not with the lawyers that represent Mr. Perisic. Is that okay?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Your Honour. Everything is clear.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Thank you so much. Court adjourned to Thursday morning at 9.00, Courtroom I.
